items.stem: Remove the seed coat of a chickpea. Now, observe the structure of the chickpea and maize seeds. Are they similar or different? Figure : Dicot and monocot seeds
items.answer: After soaking chickpea and maize seeds for two days, we observed them. Chickpea Seed: When we removed the seed coat of the chickpea, we found that the seed could be easily split into two equal halves. These two parts are the cotyledons. So, chickpea has two cotyledons. Maize Seed: The maize seed did not split into two parts like the chickpea. Even after soaking, it remained as a single piece. It has only one cotyledon. Similarities/Differences: They are different. The most obvious difference is that the chickpea seed has two cotyledons (it’s a dicot seed ), while the maize seed has only one cotyledon (it’s a monocot seed ). The chickpea seed is also more rounded, while the maize seed is flatter and somewhat shield-shaped. Activity 2.9 : Let us find out You have recorded the movement of a few animals in Table. You may have also observed how other animals move from place to place. Let us now think about the types of movement in animals. A number of animals are shown in Figure. You can add more animals that you may have observed and create a poster on the variety of animals. Which body parts are used by the animals in the poster you created and those in Figure for movement? Figure : Diversity in animals

items.stem: Share and discuss the basis of grouping you have made with other groups in your class. You will be surprised to see that the basis used by different groups may vary. What do you think are the reasons behind it? Different students might have chosen different common features for the grouping. For example, some students may have chosen the height of plants as the basis for grouping while others might have chosen presence or absence of flowers as the basis for grouping of plants (See Figure). Figure : Some possible criteria of groupings of plants and animals
items.answer: Our group collected about 30 picture cards of different plants and animals. For plants, one way we grouped them was: Plants that give flowers (e.g., rose, sunflower, hibiscus). Plants that do not give prominent flowers (or we couldn’t see them in the picture, e.g., ferns, moss, pine tree). Another way we grouped plants was by their size: Tall plants (e.g., coconut tree, mango tree). Medium-sized plants (e.g., lemon plant, rose bush). Small plants (e.g., grass, mint). For animals, one way we grouped them was by where they live: Animals that live on land (e.g., lion, elephant, dog). Animals that live in water (e.g., fish, dolphin, octopus). Animals that can fly (e.g., bird, bat, butterfly). Another way we grouped animals was by what they eat (based on our general knowledge): Animals that eat plants (e.g., cow, deer, rabbit). Animals that eat other animals (e.g., tiger, snake, eagle). When we discussed with other groups, we found they used different features for grouping. For plants, one group used “hard stem” vs “soft stem”. For animals, another group used “has fur” vs “has feathers” vs “has scales”. The reasons for these different groupings are that different groups chose different common features that they thought were important or easy to see in the pictures. There are many ways to group the same set of plants and animals depending on which characteristic you focus on. Activity 2.4 : Let us group

items.stem: Here are two types of seeds. What differences do you find among the roots and leaf venation of their plants?
items.answer: (a) Wheat plant: It has fibrous roots (many thin roots arising from the stem-base) and its leaves show parallel venation (veins run side- by-side from base to tip). (b) Kidney-bean plant: It has a tap root (one main thick root with smaller side roots) and its leaves show reticulate venation (veins form a network pattern).

items.stem: Manu’s mother maintains a kitchen garden. One day, she was digging out radish from the soil. She told Manu that radish is a kind of root. Examine a radish and write what type of root it is. What type of venation would you observe in the leaves of radish plant?
items.answer: Radish is a tap root that has become thick and fleshy to store food. The leaves of the radish plant show reticulate venation, where the veins branch and form a network.

items.stem: Look at the image of a mountain goat and a goat found in the plains. Point out the similarities and differences between them. What are the reasons for these differences?
items.answer: Aspect Mountain Goat Plain-land Goat Reason Similarities Both are mammals, have four legs, cloven hooves and eat plants (herbivores). – These are common features of goats as a species. Body build Stocky body, shorter legs but very strong muscles. Comparati- vely slimmer body, normal leg strength. Strong, short legs give better balance on steep, rocky slopes. Feet / Hooves Hooves are harder and have rough pads for gripping rocks. Hooves are smoother— good for flat ground. Adaptation for sure footing on mountains.

items.stem: Look at the image of a mountain goat and a goat found in the plains. Point out the similarities and differences between them. What are the reasons for these differences? Ans : Aspect Mountain Goat Plain-land Goat Reason Similarities Both are mammals, have four legs, cloven hooves and eat plants (herbivores). – These are common features of goats as a species. Body build Stocky body, shorter legs but very strong muscles. Comparati- vely slimmer body, normal leg strength. Strong, short legs give better balance on steep, rocky slopes. Feet / Hooves Hooves are harder and have rough pads for gripping rocks. Hooves are smoother— good for flat ground. Adaptation for sure footing on mountains.
items.answer: Yes, when we looked at the fallen leaves we collected, we noticed a lot of variation. Shape and Structure: Some leaves were long and narrow (like grass), some were broad and somewhat round (like a lotus leaf, if we had one), some were heart-shaped, and some had toothed edges (like hibiscus or rose leaflets). Some leaves were small, others were large. Some were thick, and some were thin. Veins and Venation: We observed the thin lines called veins on the leaves. In the hibiscus leaf Figure (a), the veins form a net-like pattern on both sides of a main, thick middle vein. This is called reticulate venation. In the banana leaf Figure (b), the veins run parallel to each other. This is called parallel venation. The grass leaf Figure (c) also shows veins running parallel to each other, so it also has parallel venation. So, the main difference is that in reticulate venation, the veins branch out and form a network, while in parallel venation, they run alongside each other without forming a network. items.stem: After you are done observing, make sure to replant the herbs so that they may continue to thrive and grow. What are the similarities and differences in the roots of the plants collected by you? What differences do you see in the roots of plants shown in Figure (a) and Figure (b)? Figure : Types of roots
items.answer: We went to an open area and carefully dug out a small weed (like a common broadleaf weed) and some grass, making sure to wet the soil first so the roots wouldn’t break. We washed the roots with water. Similarities and Differences in Collected Roots: The roots of the weed had one main, thick root going downwards, with smaller, thinner roots coming out from its sides. The roots of the grass looked like a bunch of many thin, similar-sized roots spreading out from the base of the stem. A similarity is that all roots help to hold the plant in the soil. Differences were in their structure – one had a main root, the other had a bushy bunch. Differences in Figure (a) and Figure (b): In Figure (a) (mustard plant), there is one main, prominent root that goes deep into the soil, and smaller roots branch off from this main root. This is called a taproot. In Figure (b) (common grass), there is no single main root. Instead, there is a cluster or bunch of many thin, fibre-like roots that arise from the base of the stem. These are called fibrous roots. After observing, we carefully replanted the herbs. Activity 2.7 : Let us relate and analyse

items.stem: Earthworm Crawls Body segments, muscles, setae (bristles)
items.answer: Animals use different body parts for movement. Ant: Walks and crawls using its legs. Goat: Walks and jumps using its legs. Pigeon: Walks using its legs and flies using its wings. Housefly: Walks using its legs and flies using its wings. Fish: Swims using its fins. Snake (from Figure): Slithers or crawls using its whole body, with the help of muscles and scales. Frog (from Figure): Hops on land using its powerful hind legs and swims in water using its legs, often with webbed feet. Earthworm (from Figure): Crawls by alternately shortening and lengthening its body segments, using muscles and tiny bristles called setae. Butterfly (from Figure): Flies using its wings. Rabbit (from Figure): Hops and runs using its legs. Tortoise (from Figure): Walks slowly using its legs. Conclusions from Table: Different animals have different ways of moving, like walking, flying, swimming, crawling, hopping, etc. They use different body parts for these movements, such as legs, wings, fins, or even their whole body. Activity 2.10 : Let us compare and analyse

items.stem: Scorpion Rhodo- dendron Sea turtle Elephant Frog
items.answer: Observations regarding plants and animals in various regions: The plants and animals found in one type of region are often very different from those found in another. In the desert: We listed Camel, Cactus, Date Palm, Desert Fox, and Scorpion. These are adapted to hot and dry conditions with little water. For example, cactus has fleshy stems to store water. Camels can survive long without water. On mountains: We listed Deodar tree, Mountain Goat, Pine tree, Yak, and Rhododendron. These are adapted to cold conditions, and sometimes snow and strong winds. Deodar trees are conical so snow slides off. Mountain goats have features for climbing. Rhododendrons on mountain tops might be shorter with smaller leaves. In the ocean: We listed Fish, Whale, Shark, Octopus, and Sea turtle. These animals are adapted to live in saltwater and have features for swimming, like fins or streamlined bodies. In the forest: We listed Lion, Tiger, Deer, Monkey, and Elephant. Forests have many trees and provide shelter and food for a variety of animals. In a pond: We listed Lotus, Tadpole, Duck, Water beetle, and Frog. These are adapted to freshwater environments. Lotus plants have leaves that float. Ducks have webbed feet for swimming. This shows that biodiversity varies greatly from region to region because the environmental conditions (like temperature, water availability, type of land) are different, and plants and animals have special features (adaptations) to survive in their specific ha you bend the stem easily, or is it stiff? Take care that the stems do not break.

items.stem: Lemon Plant Medium Brown (older parts), Green (younger parts) Hard Medium Thick Close to the ground Shrub
items.answer: During our nature walk, we observed different plants. The mango tree was much taller than us. Its stem was brown, very hard, and thick. The branches started higher up on the stem. So, it is a Tree. The rose plant was about my height (medium). Its stem was brown, hard, but thin. It had many branches starting close to the ground. So, it is a Shrub. The tomato plant was shorter than me. Its stem was green, tender (soft), and thin. Its branches also appeared close to the ground. So, it is a Herb. We also looked at grass. It was very short, with green, tender, and thin stems. It is also a Herb. A lemon plant we saw was medium height. Its older stems were brownish and hard, while newer stems were green and a bit softer. The stem was of medium thickness, and branches started near the ground. So, it is a Shrub. items.answer: Animals that can fly Animals that cannot fly Pigeon, Bat, Cockroach, Grasshopper Cow, Tortoise, Whale, Fish, Lizard

items.stem: As the population grows and people want more comfortable lives, forests are being cut down to meet various needs. How can this affect our surroundings? How do you think we can address this challenge?
items.answer: Cutting forests removes the homes of many plants and animals, reduces rainfall, causes soil to wash away, and increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the air, making Earth warmer. We can plant more trees (afforestation), save paper and wood, use recycled or alternative materials, support laws that protect forests, and spread awareness so everyone understands why trees are important.

items.stem: Analyse the flow-chart. What can be examples of ‘A’ and ‘B’?
items.answer: A (reticulate venation examples): Hibiscus, Mango, Pea. B (parallel venation examples): Wheat, Rice, Maize.

items.stem: Observe the labelled part of a duck in the picture below. What differences do you observe in the feet of the duck compared to the other birds? Which activity would the duck be able to perform using this part?
items.answer: The duck’s feet are webbed—a thin skin stretches between its toes, making each foot look like a paddle. In birds such as the pigeon, the toes are separate and end in claws for perching. Because of its webbed feet, the duck can swim efficiently; the broad surface pushes against water just like oars, helping the bird move smoothly in ponds and lakes.

items.stem: What is biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.text: The study of a single species in a specific area

options.label: B
options.text: The variety of plants and animals found in a particular region

options.label: C
options.text: The total number of animals in an ecosystem

options.label: D
options.text: The interaction between plants and their environment

items.answer: (B) The variety of plants and animals found in a particular region. Biodiversity refers to the wide range of plant and animal life present in a specific habitat or geographical area. This variety contributes to the overall health and balance of the ecosystem.

items.stem: What did Dr. Raghu advise the students to notice during the nature walk, emphasizing respect for living creatures?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the different types of trees

options.label: B
options.text: The variety of smells and to observe without disturbing

options.label: C
options.text: The colors of the flowers exclusively

options.label: D
options.text: The number of insects they could find

items.answer: (B) The variety of smells and to observe without disturbing. Dr. Raghu advised the students to notice the variety of smells in the park and emphasized respecting all living creatures by observing them without causing any disturbance during their nature walk.

items.stem: Why is grouping plants and animals important in science?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes it harder to study individual species

options.label: B
options.text: It primarily helps in naming new organisms

options.label: C
options.text: It makes it easier to understand and study them based on similarities and differences

options.label: D
options.text: It is only useful for creating museum exhibits

items.answer: (C) It makes it easier to understand and study them based on similarities and differences. Grouping organisms based on shared characteristics (similarities) and distinguishing features (differences) helps in organizing the vast diversity of life, making it more manageable to study and understand relationships between different organisms.

items.stem: What are plants with soft, green, and tender stems, typically small in size, called?
items.answer: (C) Herbs Herbs are characterized by their relatively small size and stems that are soft, green, and tender. Tomato plants are an example of herbs.

items.stem: Which of the following plants is an example of a shrub?
items.answer: (C) Rose plant The shrubs as plants that are not as tall as trees, often with many brown woody stems branching near the ground. A rose plant is cited as an example.

items.stem: What is the primary basis for classifying plants into herbs, shrubs, and trees?

options.label: A
options.text: The color and shape of their flowers

options.label: B
options.text: The height and nature of their stems

options.label: C
options.text: The type of fruits they produce

options.label: D
options.text: The environment in which they grow

items.answer: (B) The height and nature of their stems. On observing plant height and stem characteristics (like hardness, thickness, and branching patterns) to group them into herbs, shrubs, or trees.

items.stem: What is venation in leaves?

options.label: A
options.text: The color pattern on the leaf surface

options.label: C
options.text: The pattern of veins on the leaf

options.label: D
options.text: The way leaves are attached to the stem

items.answer: (C) The pattern of veins on the leaf. Venation refers to the arrangement or pattern of veins, which are thin lines visible on the surface of a leaf. These veins are crucial for transporting water and nutrients.

items.stem: What is the main difference between reticulate venation and parallel venation in leaves?

options.label: A
options.text: Reticulate venation has veins parallel to each other, while parallel venation has a net-like pattern

options.label: B
options.text: Reticulate venation is found in grasses, while parallel venation is found in hibiscus

options.label: C
options.text: Reticulate venation forms a net-like pattern, while parallel venation has veins running parallel

options.label: D
options.text: Reticulate venation refers to thick veins, while parallel venation refers to thin veins

items.answer: (C) Reticulate venation forms a net-like pattern, while parallel venation has veins running parallel. Reticulate venation is characterized by a web- like or net-like arrangement of veins, as seen in hibiscus leaves. Parallel venation features veins that run parallel to one another, typical of banana or grass leaves.

items.stem: What type of root system consists of one main root with smaller side roots arising from it?
items.answer: (B) Taproot system A taproot system is characterized by a prominent, central main root (the taproot) from which smaller, lateral roots branch out. The mustard plant is an example of this.

items.stem: Which type of root system is generally found in common grass plants?
items.answer: (B) Fibrous root system Common grass plants typically have a fibrous root system, where a bunch of similar-sized, thin roots arise from the base of the stem, rather than having a single main root.

items.stem: What general relationship is observed between leaf venation and the type of root system in plants?

options.label: A
options.text: Plants with reticulate venation usually have fibrous roots

options.label: B
options.text: Plants with parallel venation usually have taproots

options.label: C
options.text: Plants with reticulate venation usually have taproots, and those with parallel venation usually have fibrous roots

options.label: D
options.text: There is no general relationship between leaf venation and root type

items.answer: (C) Plants with reticulate venation usually have taproots, and those with parallel venation usually have fibrous roots. There is a general pattern where plants with reticulate (net-like) venation usually have taproots, while those with parallel venation typically have fibrous root systems.

items.stem: What are cotyledons?

options.label: A
options.text: The first leaves that emerge from a seed

options.label: B
options.text: The protective outer covering of a seed

options.label: C
options.text: The parts of a seed that can sometimes be split, like in a chickpea

options.label: D
options.text: The small roots that develop from a germinating seed

items.answer: (C) The parts of a seed that can sometimes be split, like in a chickpea. Cotyledons are embryonic leaves within a seed. In dicotyledonous plants like chickpeas, the seed can be split into two such parts. They often store food for the embryo.

items.stem: How many cotyledons does a maize seed typically have?
items.answer: (B) One (single thin cotyledon) Maize is an example of a monocotyledonous plant, meaning its seeds contain a single, often thin, cotyledon.

items.stem: What are the typical characteristics of dicot plants regarding their leaf venation and root system?

options.label: A
options.text: Parallel venation and fibrous root system

options.label: B
options.text: Reticulate venation and fibrous root system

items.answer: (D) Reticulate venation and taproot system. Dicotyledonous (dicot) plants generally exhibit reticulate venation in their leaves and possess a taproot system, where there’s a main central root.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a main feature used to classify animals?

options.label: A
options.text: The type of movement they exhibit

options.label: B
options.text: The body parts they use for movement

items.answer: (C) The sounds they make. Although bird chirps are mentioned as an example of diversity, animals are mainly grouped based on how they move, the body parts they use for movement, and their habitats not primarily by the sounds they make.

items.stem: How would you categorize the fact that a fish uses its fins to swim in water?

options.label: B
options.text: Type of movement and body parts used for movement

options.label: C
options.text: Color and size of the animal

items.answer: (B) Type of movement and body parts used for movement. The statement “a fish uses its fins to swim in water” relates directly to how the animal moves (swimming) and which body parts it uses for that movement (fins). This fits under the category of type of movement and body parts used for movement, making option (B) the correct choice.

items.stem: What are adaptations?

options.label: A
options.text: The scientific names given to plants and animals

options.label: B
options.text: The general behaviors common to all living organisms

options.label: C
options.text: Special features that enable plants and animals to survive in a particular region

options.label: D
options.text: The diseases that affect plants and animals in specific habitats

items.answer: (C) Special features that enable plants and animals to survive in a particular region. Adaptations are specific physical or behavioral characteristics that have evolved in organisms, allowing them to live successfully and reproduce in their particular environment or habitat.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of a terrestrial habitat?
items.answer: (C) Forests Terrestrial habitats are defined as places where plants and animals live on land, with forests given as one example of this type of habitat.

items.stem: Why does the biodiversity of a hot desert differ significantly from that of a cold mountainous region?

options.label: A
options.text: Because animals in deserts are always larger

options.label: B
options.text: Because plants in mountains do not need water

options.label: C
options.text: Because plants and animals have different adaptations to survive the distinct environmental conditions

options.label: D
options.text: Because all species prefer mountainous regions for their beauty

items.answer: (C) Because plants and animals have different adaptations to survive the distinct environmental conditions. Different regions have vastly different environmental conditions (e.g., temperature, water availability). Organisms living in these regions possess specific adaptations (special features) that help them survive those particular conditions, leading to diverse forms of life.

items.stem: What is a habitat?

options.label: A
options.text: The food that an animal eats

options.label: B
options.text: The place where plants and animals live

options.label: D
options.text: The group to which a plant belongs

items.answer: (B) The place where plants and animals live. A habitat is the natural environment or home of a plant, animal, or other organism. It provides the resources necessary for survival, such as food, water, and shelter.

items.stem: What unique feature helps deodar trees survive in snowy mountainous regions?

options.label: A
options.text: They have very deep root systems

options.label: B
options.text: They produce brightly colored flowers to attract pollinators

options.label: C
options.text: Their conical shape and sloping branches allow snow to slide off easily

options.label: D
options.text: Their leaves are very thick and store a lot of water

items.answer: (C) Their conical shape and sloping branches allow snow to slide off easily. Deodar trees, found in mountainous regions with snowfall, have a conical shape and flexible, sloping branches. This structure is an adaptation that helps prevent snow accumulation, allowing them to survive such conditions.

items.stem: How does the damage to habitats lead to a loss of biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.text: It forces animals to learn new ways of finding food

options.label: B
options.text: It results in the loss of homes, food, and other resources for plants and animals

options.label: C
options.text: It primarily affects only the plant populations

options.label: D
options.text: It causes animals to migrate to more populated areas

items.answer: (B) It results in the loss of homes, food, and other resources for plants and animals. When habitats are damaged or destroyed, the plants and animals that depend on those habitats for survival lose their homes, food sources, and other essential resources, which can lead to a decline in their populations and ultimately, a loss of biodiversity.

items.stem: What was the name of the movement that began in the early 1970s in Uttarakhand to stop the cutting of trees?
items.answer: (C) Chipko movement The Chipko movement, which began in the early 1970s in Uttarakhand, was a significant environmental movement where local people, especially women, hugged trees to protect them from being felled, thus saving forests.

items.stem: What are sacred groves ?

options.label: A
options.text: Gardens specifically designed for growing medicinal plants

options.label: B
options.text: Man-made forests planted for commercial purposes

options.label: C
options.text: Undisturbed patches of forests protected by local communities

options.label: D
options.text: Areas designated for scientific research on trees

items.answer: (C) Undisturbed patches of forests protected by local communities. Sacred groves are traditionally protected patches of forest that are preserved by local communities, often due to religious or cultural beliefs. These areas harbor rich biodiversity because human interference is typically restricted.

items.stem: Who is referred to as the ‘Birdman of India’?
items.answer: (C) Salim Ali Salim Ali, an eminent ornithologist, is known as the ‘Birdman of India’ for his extensive work on observing, documenting and conserving bird diversity across India.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example that illustrates the interdependence between plants and animals?

options.label: B
options.text: Animals helping in spreading seeds after eating fruits

options.label: C
options.text: Birds building nests on trees without benefiting the tree

options.label: D
options.text: Different animal species competing for the same food source

items.answer: (B) Animals helping in spreading seeds after eating fruits. When animals consume fruits and then disperse the seeds through their droppings, they help in the propagation of plants. This is a clear example of the mutual dependence between plants and animals.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a tree?

options.label: B
options.text: Has soft, green, and tender stems

options.label: C
options.text: Has hard, thick, brown, and woody stems

options.label: D
options.text: Branches typically start higher up on the stem

items.answer: (B) Has soft, green, and tender stems. Trees are characterized by their height, and hard, thick, woody stems. Soft, green, and tender stems are characteristic of herbs, not trees.

items.stem: How do climbers and creepers differ in their growth habit?

options.label: A
options.text: Climbers grow tall independently, while creepers need support

options.label: B
options.text: Climbers creep along the ground, while creepers need support to climb

options.label: C
options.text: Climbers need support to climb and grow, while creepers spread along the ground

options.label: D
options.text: Both climbers and creepers have very strong, woody stems

items.answer: (C) Climbers need support to climb and grow, while creepers spread along the ground. Plants with weak stems that use external support to grow upwards are called climbers. Plants that spread out horizontally along the ground are known as creepers.

items.stem: A student observes a plant with leaves showing a net-like pattern of veins. Based on the information, what type of root system is this plant most likely to have?
items.answer: (B) Taproot system It is generally observed that plants with reticulate (net-like) venation in their leaves, such as the rose (a dicot), usually have a taproot system—showing a common pattern in plant structure.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Camels found in hot deserts excrete small amounts of urine and have dry dung. Reason (R) : These features are adaptations to conserve water in arid environments.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Camels in hot deserts producing concentrated urine and dry dung are crucial adaptations. These mechanisms minimize water loss, which is essential for survival in environments where water is scarce.

items.stem: Damage to habitats does not affect biodiversity. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.answer: (B) 2 only Biodiversity includes the variety of both plants and animals. Each organism plays a role in its ecosystem. Habitat damage directly leads to loss of biodiversity. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct.

items.stem: During a nature walk, students are asked to group plants based on their stem characteristics. One plant is observed to be medium height with several hard, brown, woody stems branching out near the ground. Into which group would this plant most likely be classified?
items.answer: (B) Shrub Shrubs are described as plants of medium height with hard, woody stems that branch near the ground, which matches the description of a hibiscus plant.

items.stem: The Botanical Survey of India was headed by an Indian botanist who initiated programs to document plant diversity. Who was this botanist?
items.answer: (C) Janaki Ammal Janaki Ammal, as the head of the Botanical Survey of India, played a crucial role in initiating programs to document the plant diversity of India, contributing significantly to its preservation.

items.stem: Why are amphibians like frogs considered to have a unique habitat requirement compared to fish or goats?

options.label: A
options.text: They only live in very cold environments

options.label: B
options.text: They can live in water as well as on land

options.label: C
options.text: They exclusively live on tall trees

options.label: D
options.text: They only consume insects for food

items.answer: (B) They can live in water as well as on land. Amphibians, such as frogs, are adapted to live both in aquatic environments (like water for breeding and early life stages) and terrestrial environments (on land). This dual habitat is a distinguishing characteristic.

items.stem: What are plants called that have seeds with two cotyledons?
items.answer: (B) Dicotyledons (dicots) Plants whose seeds possess two cotyledons (embryonic leaves) are classified as dicotyledons, often shortened to dicots. Chickpeas are an example of dicots.

items.stem: ‘Project Tiger’ was initiated in India in which year?
items.answer: (B) 1973 ‘Project Tiger’ was launched in 1973 by the Government of India to protect the rapidly declining population of the Bengal Tiger.

items.stem: Which feature distinguishes the stem of a tree from the stem of a herb?

options.label: A
options.text: Tree stems are always green, while herb stems are brown

options.label: B
options.text: Tree stems are hard, thick, and woody, while herb stems are soft and green

options.label: C
options.text: Tree stems branch from the base, while herb stems do not branch

options.label: D
options.text: Tree stems are shorter than herb stems

items.answer: (B) Tree stems are hard, thick, and woody, while herb stems are soft and green. Trees typically have tall, hard, thick, brown, and woody stems, whereas herbs are characterized by their small size and soft, green stems.

items.stem: All of the following are mentioned as features that vary among different plants EXCEPT:
items.answer: (D) The ability to perform photosynthesis. While height, leaf characteristics, and flower attributes are discussed as varying features for grouping plants, the fundamental ability to perform photosynthesis is a common characteristic of most plants, not a primary basis for the initial groupings discussed.

items.stem: If you find a plant with leaves that have veins running parallel to each other, what kind of root system would you generally expect it to have?

options.label: C
options.text: A combination of taproot and fibrous roots

items.answer: (B) Fibrous root system There is a general correlation that plants with parallel venation in their leaves, like grasses and other monocots, typically have a fibrous root system.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : The biodiversity of different regions varies. Reason (R) : Different regions have distinct environmental conditions, and plants and animals possess adaptations to survive in those specific conditions.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. The variation in environmental factors across different regions (like deserts versus mountains) necessitates different survival strategies. Organisms develop specific adaptations to thrive in their particular habitats, leading to the observed differences in biodiversity.

items.stem: What term is used to describe animals that can live both in water and on land?
items.answer: (C) Amphibians Animals, such as frogs, that are adapted to live and survive in both aquatic (water) and terrestrial (land) environments are classified as amphibians.

items.stem: Which plant is mentioned as having a taproot system and reticulate venation, similar to sadabahar?
items.answer: (C) Chickpea (chana) Chickpea (chana) is an example of a plant that has a taproot system and exhibits reticulate venation in its leaves—both features typical of dicot plants.

items.stem: Why is it important to protect biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.text: To ensure there are enough animals for zoos

options.label: B
options.text: To make sure our planet is full of life, helping plants and animals survive and thrive

options.label: C
options.text: Primarily to increase the number of plant species for human consumption

options.label: D
options.text: To prevent animals from migrating to new habitats

items.answer: (B) To make sure our planet is full of life, helping plants and animals survive and thrive. Protecting biodiversity is crucial for maintaining healthy ecosystems where diverse species can survive and flourish. This ensures ecological balance and the continuation of life in its varied forms on Earth.

items.stem: What is the term for the method of arranging things into groups based on their common features?
items.answer: (B) Grouping Grouping, or classification, is the process of organizing or arranging items, including plants and animals, into distinct categories based on shared characteristics or common features. This simplifies study and understanding.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as an example of a terrestrial habitat?
items.answer: (D) Ponds Ponds are listed as examples of aquatic habitats, which are environments where organisms live in water. Forests, deserts, and grasslands are examples of terrestrial (land-based) habitats.

items.stem: What is a key difference in the humps of camels from hot deserts compared to those from cold deserts?

options.label: A
options.text: Hot desert camels have no humps, cold desert camels have one

options.label: B
options.text: Hot desert camels have two humps, cold desert camels have one

options.label: C
options.text: Hot desert camels have one hump, cold desert camels have two humps

options.label: D
options.text: Both types of camels have the same number of humps

items.answer: (C) Hot desert camels have one hump, cold desert camels have two humps. Camels living in hot deserts usually have one hump to store food, while those in cold desert regions like Ladakh typically have two humps for the same purpose.

items.stem: A student observes an animal that both flies and walks. Which of the following animals best fits this description of movement?
items.answer: (C) Pigeon The pigeon as an animal that exhibits both flying and walking as types of movement, using its wings and legs respectively.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : The streamlined body of a fish is an adaptation. Reason (R) : This body shape helps the fish to swim efficiently in water.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A fish’s streamlined body is a specific feature (adaptation) that reduces water resistance, enabling it to move through water with greater ease and efficiency. This shows a direct link between the feature and its function for survival in its habitat.

items.stem: Seeds with two cotyledons. Which of these characteristics are generally associated with dicot plants?
items.answer: (C) 1 and 3 only Dicot plants are typically characterized by the presence of a taproot system and seeds that contain two cotyledons. Parallel venation is generally a feature of monocot plants.

items.stem: A remote village community strictly prohibits the cutting of trees and harming animals within a specific forested area near their settlement, believing it to be sacred. This protected area is an example of a:
items.answer: (B) Sacred grove Sacred groves are patches of forest traditionally protected by local communities, often due to cultural or religious significance. The scenario describes such a community-protected area where harming nature is disallowed, fitting the description of a sacred grove.

items.stem: What is the main objective of a nature walk for students?

options.label: A
options.text: To collect as many different plant specimens as possible

options.label: B
options.text: To identify and name all plants and animals encountered

options.label: C
options.text: To experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals in nature

options.label: D
options.text: To measure the height and width of the trees in the area

items.answer: (C) To experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals in nature. Dr. Raghu informed the students that the objective of the nature walk was to experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals present in their natural surroundings.

items.stem: How does Maniram chacha’s skill of mimicking bird calls contribute to the students’ learning during the nature walk?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps in scaring away other animals

options.label: B
options.text: It demonstrates an example of diversity in nature (unique bird chirps)

options.label: C
options.text: It is primarily for entertainment purposes

options.label: D
options.text: It helps in attracting birds for closer observation

items.answer: (B) It demonstrates an example of diversity in nature (unique bird chirps). After Dr. Raghu mentioned that each bird has a unique chirp as an example of diversity, Maniram chacha mimicking different bird calls would further illustrate this diversity in bird vocalizations.

items.stem: Plants that are not as tall as trees, often with many brown woody stems starting close to the ground, are called:
items.answer: (B) Shrubs Shrubs are defined as plants that are usually shorter than trees and have several hard, woody stems that branch out near the base.

items.stem: What is a key difference in the stems of herbs versus shrubs?

options.label: A
options.text: Herb stems are brown and woody; shrub stems are green and soft

options.label: B
options.text: Herb stems are soft and green; shrub stems are brown and woody (though not as thick as trees)

options.label: C
options.text: Herbs have a single main stem; shrubs have no stems

options.label: D
options.text: Herb stems branch high up; shrub stems branch near the ground

items.answer: (B) Herb stems are soft and green; shrub stems are brown and woody (though not as thick as trees). Herbs are characterized by soft, green, and tender stems, while shrubs typically have multiple brown, woody stems that are harder but not as thick as those of trees.

items.stem: The several ways in which animals move. Which of the following is NOT specifically mentioned as a type of animal movement?
items.answer: (C) Hibernate The movements like flying, walking, jumping, and crawling. Hibernation is a state of inactivity and metabolic depression, not a method of locomotion.

items.stem: A student finds a plant with a single main root from which smaller roots are growing. Its leaves show a net-like vein pattern. This plant is most likely a:
items.answer: (B) Dicot with reticulate venation. A single main root (taproot) and net-like leaf venation (reticulate venation) are characteristic features generally associated with dicotyledonous plants.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Camels living in cold deserts like Ladakh grow long hair from head to neck. Reason (R) : This long hair is an adaptation that helps them survive the cold winter temperatures.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. The growth of long hair on camels in cold deserts is a specific physical feature (adaptation). This thick coat of hair provides insulation, helping the animal to conserve body heat and survive the extremely cold temperatures of its habitat.

items.stem: The number of cotyledons in a seed is a basis for grouping plants.
items.answer: (C) 1 and 3 only Plants are grouped into herbs, shrubs, and trees based on stem characteristics and height. They are also grouped into monocots and dicots based on the number of cotyledons. Leaf venation type varies and is not solely determined by leaf color.

items.stem: A farmer is growing wheat in his field. Wheat grains, when examined, show a single cotyledon. where the veins run alongside each other from base to tip. What type of leaf venation and root system would the wheat plants likely exhibit?

options.label: B
options.text: Parallel venation and fibrous root system

options.label: C
options.text: Reticulate venation and fibrous root system

items.answer: (B) Parallel venation and fibrous root system. Wheat is a monocot (single cotyledon). Monocots generally have parallel venation in their leaves and a fibrous root system, which aligns with the scenario’s observation.

items.stem: The ‘Cheetah Reintroduction Project’ was initiated in India in which year?
items.answer: (C) 2022 The ‘Cheetah Reintroduction Project’ was launched in 2022 to help restore the population of cheetahs in India.

items.stem: Why is it advised not to pluck leaves and flowers during a nature walk?

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure they remain for others to observe and for their ecological role

options.label: C
options.text: Because it is difficult to carry them back

options.label: D
options.text: Because they wilt quickly after being plucked

items.answer: (B) To ensure they remain for others to observe and for their ecological role. Not plucking leaves and flowers during a nature walk is a way to respect nature, ensure that these parts of the plant remain for their natural functions (like photosynthesis or reproduction), and allow others to observe them.

items.stem: Which term describes plants that typically have a main root from which smaller, side roots grow?
items.answer: (B) Taproot A taproot is the main, central root of a plant from which lateral or side roots branch off. This is characteristic of a taproot system.

items.stem: What kind of leaf venation is exhibited by the leaves of a banana plant?
items.answer: (B) Parallel venation Banana plant leaves show parallel venation, with veins running side by side along the length of the leaf.

items.stem: What is the primary difference between terrestrial and aquatic habitats?

options.label: A
options.text: Terrestrial habitats are always hot, and aquatic habitats are always cold

options.label: B
options.text: Terrestrial habitats are on land, and aquatic habitats are in water

options.label: C
options.text: Terrestrial habitats have only plants, and aquatic habitats have only animals

options.label: D
options.text: Terrestrial habitats are man-made, and aquatic habitats are natural

items.answer: (B) Terrestrial habitats are on land, and aquatic habitats are in water. The fundamental distinction is that terrestrial habitats are land-based environments (like forests, deserts), while aquatic habitats are water-based environments (like ponds, oceans).

items.stem: All of the following are listed as examples of animals that have declined in India due to loss of natural habitats EXCEPT:
items.answer: (D) Common Crow The Bengal Tiger, Cheetah, and Great Indian Bustard are species whose populations have declined due to habitat loss. The common crow is not mentioned in this context.

items.stem: If a plant has leaves with a net-like pattern of veins and its seeds can be split into two distinct halves, it is likely a:
items.answer: (B) Dicot with taproots. Net-like (reticulate) venation and seeds with two halves (dicotyledonous) are characteristic features of dicot plants, which also typically have taproot systems.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Sacred groves are important for conserving biodiversity. Reason (R) : Local communities protect these forest patches, preventing harm to plants and animals within them.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Sacred groves contribute to biodiversity conservation precisely because the protection provided by local communities restricts harmful activities like tree cutting and animal harm, allowing diverse species to thrive undisturbed.

items.stem: It is generally much taller than herbs and shrubs.
items.answer: (C) 1 and 3 only Trees are characterized by tall stature and hard, thick, woody stems. Their branches typically originate higher up on the stem, unlike shrubs where branching is near the ground.

items.stem: A scientist is studying a newly discovered plant. The plant’s seeds have only one cotyledon. The leaves show veins that run parallel to the midrib. Based on these observations, the plant most likely has:
items.answer: (B) A fibrous root system. Plants with seeds containing a single cotyledon (monocots) and leaves exhibiting parallel venation generally possess a fibrous root system.

items.stem: The ‘Save Silent Valley’ movement was primarily aimed at preventing the construction of what?

options.label: B
options.text: A hydroelectric dam across the Kunthipuzha river

options.label: C
options.text: A new highway through the forest

items.answer: (B) A hydroelectric dam across the Kunthipuzha river. The Save Silent Valley movement was a significant effort to prevent the construction of a proposed hydroelectric dam across the Kunthipuzha river, which would have submerged a large area of the pristine forest.

items.stem: How do the wide hooves of a camel living in a hot sandy desert provide an advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: They help the camel to dig for water

options.label: B
options.text: They help the camel to walk on sand without sinking

options.label: C
options.text: They keep the camel cool by radiating excess heat

options.label: D
options.text: They are used for defense against predators

items.answer: (B) They help the camel to walk on sand without sinking. The wide hooves of a desert camel distribute its weight over a larger area of sand. This prevents the camel from sinking into the loose sand, making it easier to walk in its desert habitat.

items.stem: What is the general term for the place where different types of plants and animals are found living together, sharing resources?
items.answer: (B) Habitat A habitat is the natural home or environment of an organism, where it lives and finds the resources it needs like food, water, and shelter. Many different species can share the same habitat.

items.stem: In the context of plants, what does “dicot” stand for?
items.answer: (B) Having seeds with two cotyledons. “Dicot” is short for dicotyledon, which refers to plants whose seeds have two embryonic leaves, or cotyledons.

items.stem: How does the stem of a shrub typically differ from the stem of a tree?

options.label: A
options.text: Shrub stems are soft and green, while tree stems are hard and woody

options.label: B
options.text: Shrub stems are generally thicker and taller than tree stems

options.label: C
options.text: Shrub stems are hard and woody but usually not as thick as tree stems, and they branch near the ground

options.label: D
options.text: Shrubs have a single main stem, while trees have multiple stems from the base

items.answer: (C) Shrub stems are hard and woody but usually not as thick as tree stems, and they branch near the ground. Shrubs have hard, woody stems like trees, but they are typically not as thick and tend to branch out closer to the ground level, unlike trees which usually have a main trunk with branches higher up.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way animals move in Table?
items.answer: (D) Photosynthesizes The types of physical movement animals use for locomotion, such as walking, flying, and swimming (implied for fish). Photosynthesis is a process of food production in plants, not a type of animal movement.

items.stem: If a plant exhibits parallel venation in its leaves and its seeds contain a single cotyledon, what type of root system is it most likely to possess?

options.label: C
options.text: A deep main root with few branches

items.answer: (B) Fibrous root system These characteristics – parallel venation and a single cotyledon – are typical of monocot plants, which generally have a fibrous root system.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : The diversity of plants and animals varies from region to region. Reason (R) : All regions on Earth have identical climatic conditions and resources.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (C) A is true, but R is false. It is true that biodiversity varies across regions. However, the reason for this variation is the presence of diverse, not identical, climatic conditions and resources, to which organisms adapt.

items.stem: Hard, thick, brown, and woody stems. Which of these features are characteristic of herbs?
items.answer: (A) 1 and 2 only Herbs are generally small plants characterized by soft and green stems. Hard, thick, brown, and woody stems are features of trees and shrubs.

items.stem: A group of students is studying a tall plant with a thick, woody main stem from which branches emerge high above the ground. Its leaves show a net-like pattern of veins.This plant would be classified as a:

options.label: B
options.text: Shrub with a fibrous root system

items.answer: (C) Tree with a taproot system. The description matches that of a tree (tall, thick woody stem, branches high up). Net-like venation suggests it’s a dicot, which typically has a taproot system.

items.stem: What is the primary role of the ‘Cheetah Reintroduction Project’ in India?

options.label: A
options.text: To study the behavior of cheetahs in captivity

options.label: B
options.text: To train cheetahs for wildlife safaris

options.label: C
options.text: To restore the population of the Cheetah in India

options.label: D
options.text: To export cheetahs to other countries

items.answer: (C) To restore the population of the Cheetah in India. The ‘Cheetah Reintroduction Project’ was launched in India to restore the country’s cheetah population, which had previously become extinct.

items.stem: Who were invited to the school by Madam Sulekha for a nature walk?
items.answer: Dr Raghu and Maniram chacha.

items.stem: What is Maniram chacha an expert in, related to birds?
items.answer: Mimicking bird calls.

items.stem: What was the stated objective of the nature walk for the students?
items.answer: To experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals in nature.

items.stem: What did Dr Raghu inform the students about each bird’s chirp?
items.answer: Each bird has a unique chirp.

items.stem: What term is used for the variety of plants and animals found in a particular region?
items.answer: Biodiversity.

items.stem: Are plants and animals dependent on each other according to the chapter?
items.answer: Yes.

items.stem: What is the general term for plants that are typically small with soft and green stems?
items.answer: Herbs.

items.stem: What is the pattern of veins on a leaf called?
items.answer: Venation.

items.stem: What type of venation has a net-like pattern on both sides of a thick middle vein?
items.answer: Reticulate venation.

items.stem: What type of roots appear as a bunch of similar- sized thin roots from the base of the stem?
items.answer: Fibrous roots.

items.stem: Generally, what type of roots do plants with reticulate venation have?
items.answer: Taproots.

items.stem: How many cotyledons do dicotyledon (dicot) plants have in their seeds?
items.answer: Two cotyledons.

items.stem: What type of root system do monocot plants generally have?
items.answer: Fibrous root system.

items.stem: What are the special features that enable plants and animals to survive in a particular region called?
items.answer: Adaptations.

items.stem: What is the place where plants and animals live called?
items.answer: Habitat.

items.stem: Give one example of a terrestrial habitat mentioned in the chapter.
items.answer: Forests (or deserts, grasslands, mountains).

items.stem: What are animals called that can live both in water and on land?
items.answer: Amphibians.

items.stem: What was the name of the project initiated in 1973 to protect the Bengal Tiger?
items.answer: Project Tiger.

items.stem: What are traditionally protected patches of forests, guarded by local communities, called?
items.answer: Sacred groves.

items.stem: What advice did Dr Raghu give the students about observing living creatures during the nature walk?
items.answer: Dr Raghu advised students to notice the variety of smells and emphasized respecting all living creatures, observing them without any disturbance.

items.stem: List three ways plants can vary as observed by the students.
items.answer: Plants can vary by being tall/short with hard/ soft stems, having different leaf shapes and arrangements, and flowers varying in color, shape, and scent.

items.stem: How do animals depend on plants, and plants on animals? Give one example for each.
items.answer: Trees provide food and shelter to animals; animals help in spreading seeds after eating fruits, showing mutual dependence for survival and propagation.

items.stem: Why is grouping plants and animals important ?
items.answer: Grouping plants and animals based on their similarities and differences makes it easier to understand and study their vast diversity systematically.

items.stem: Describe the main characteristics of shrubs as per the chapter.
items.answer: Shrubs are not as tall as trees, often have many brown woody stems branching close to the ground, which are hard but not very thick.

items.stem: What is the difference between climbers and creepers?
items.answer: Climbers are plants with weak stems that need support to climb and grow upwards, while creepers are plants that spread along the ground.

items.stem: Explain parallel venation with an example given in the chapter.
items.answer: In parallel venation, the veins on a leaf run parallel to each other. For example, the leaves of banana plants and grasses exhibit this pattern.

items.stem: What is a taproot system? Give an example of a plant with a taproot.
items.answer: A taproot system consists of one main root with smaller side roots arising from it. A mustard plant or hibiscus has a taproot system.

items.stem: What is the general relationship between the number of cotyledons in a seed and its leaf venation type?
items.answer: Dicot plants, with two cotyledons, generally have reticulate venation, while monocot plants, with one cotyledon, generally have parallel venation in their leaves.

items.stem: How did Janaki Ammal contribute to preserving India’s plant biodiversity?
items.answer: Janaki Ammal documented and worked to preserve India’s rich plant biodiversity and played a key role in the ‘Save Silent Valley’ movement.

items.stem: What are two distinct features of deodar trees that help them survive in snowy mountains?
items.answer: Deodar trees are conical in shape and have flexible, sloping branches, which help them to let snow slide off easily in mountainous regions.

items.stem: How do the fleshy stems of desert plants help them survive?
items.answer: The fleshy stems of desert plants, like cacti, can store water, which helps these plants tolerate and survive the hot and dry desert conditions.

items.stem: Mention two differences between camels found in hot deserts and those in cold deserts.
items.answer: Hot desert camels have one hump and long legs, while cold desert camels have two humps and comparatively shorter legs with long hair.

items.stem: How do camels in hot deserts conserve water?
items.answer: Camels in hot deserts conserve water by excreting small amounts of urine, having dry dung, and not sweating much, allowing survival without water for days.

items.stem: Define “habitat” and provide an example from the chapter.
items.answer: A habitat is the place where plants and animals live, providing them with food, water, air, and shelter. For example, a camel’s habitat is the desert.

items.stem: Differentiate between terrestrial and aquatic habitats, giving one example of each ?
items.answer: Terrestrial habitats are on land, like forests where lions live. Aquatic habitats are in water, like oceans where fish live.

items.stem: Why has the population of the Bengal Tiger declined in India?
items.answer: The population of the Bengal Tiger has declined in India primarily due to the loss of its natural habitat caused by human activities.

items.stem: What is a key characteristic of sacred groves that helps protect biodiversity?
items.answer: Sacred groves are protected by the local community, where no one is allowed to harm animals or cut trees, thus preserving them as community-protected biodiversity treasures.

items.stem: What is the main consequence of damage to the habitats of plants and animals?
items.answer: Damage to habitats results in plants and animals losing their homes, food, and other resources, ultimately leading to a loss of biodiversity.

items.stem: What was the purpose of a nature walk and what key instructions were given to the students to ensure a respectful and fruitful learning experience?
items.answer: The purpose of the nature walk was to help students experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals in nature. Key instructions included carrying a notebook and pen for recording observations, noticing the variety of smells, respecting all living creatures by observing them without disturbance, carefully listening to different sounds, and not plucking leaves or flowers. This approach aimed to foster observation skills while instilling respect for nature and its biodiversity.

items.stem: Explain the concept of biodiversity. Why is there variation in biodiversity from one region to another? Use examples of plants from different regions.
items.answer: Biodiversity refers to the variety of plants and animals found in a particular region. This variation exists because different regions have distinct environmental conditions. For instance, cactus plants with thick, fleshy stems are found in deserts to store scarce water, while deodar trees in cold mountains are conical with sloping branches to let snow slide off easily. Rhododendrons in the Nilgiris are shorter with smaller leaves to survive heavy winds, unlike taller ones in Sikkim. These adaptations to local conditions shape regional biodiversity.

items.stem: The grouping plants based on several characteristics. Describe how plants are classified into herbs, shrubs, and trees, highlighting the distinguishing features of each group.
items.answer: Plants are grouped into herbs, shrubs, and trees based on height and stem characteristics. Herbs are typically small with soft, green stems. Shrubs are medium-sized, not as tall as trees, often with multiple hard, woody brown stems that branch near the ground but aren’t very thick. Trees are tall plants with hard, thick, brown woody stems, and their branches usually start higher up on the stem, away from the ground. This classification helps in understanding plant diversity.

items.stem: Explain the two main types of leaf venation discussed in the chapter: reticulate and parallel. Provide an example for each type.
items.answer: Leaf venation is the pattern of veins on a leaf. Reticulate venation shows a net-like pattern of veins on both sides of a thick middle vein; for example, hibiscus leaves exhibit this. Parallel venation is where the veins run parallel to each other along the length of the leaf; examples include the leaves of banana plants and grasses. Observing venation is one way to group and identify different types of plants and understand their structural diversity.

items.stem: Describe the two primary types of root systems found in plants – taproot and fibrous root. What is the general correlation observed between root type and leaf venation?
items.answer: A taproot system consists of one main, prominent root with smaller, lateral roots branching off it, like in a mustard plant. A fibrous root system appears as a bunch of many thin, similar-sized roots arising from the base of the stem, as seen in common grass. Generally, plants exhibiting reticulate leaf venation, such as hibiscus or chickpea, tend to have taproots, while those with parallel leaf venation, like lemongrass or wheat, usually possess fibrous roots.

items.stem: What are monocotyledonous (monocot) and dicotyledonous (dicot) plants? Explain the key differences between them based on seeds, leaf venation, and root systems.
items.answer: Plants are classified as monocots or dicots based on the number of cotyledons in their seeds. Dicot plants have seeds with two cotyledons (e.g., chickpea), typically exhibit reticulate leaf venation, and possess a taproot system. Monocot plants have seeds with a single cotyledon (e.g., maize), generally show parallel leaf venation, and have a fibrous root system. These correlated features help in the broad classification of flowering plants.

items.stem: Define “adaptations” in the context of plants and animals. Provide two specific examples of animal adaptations from the chapter, explaining how each feature helps the animal survive in its particular habitat.
items.answer: Adaptations are special features that enable plants and animals to survive in a particular region or habitat. For example, fish have streamlined bodies and fins which are adaptations for easy movement in their aquatic habitat. Camels in hot deserts have long legs with wide hooves to walk on sand without sinking, and they can store food in humps and conserve water, which are crucial adaptations for survival in arid conditions with scarce resources.

items.stem: What does a habitat provide to plants and animals? What are the consequences of habitat damage, and why is it crucial to protect biodiversity?
items.answer: A habitat is the natural living place of plants and animals, providing them with essential needs like food, water, air, and shelter for their survival. Damage to habitats, often due to human activities, leads to the loss of these resources, causing displacement or death of organisms and ultimately resulting in a loss of biodiversity. Protecting biodiversity is crucial to ensure our planet remains full of life, allowing diverse species to survive, thrive, and maintain ecological balance.

items.stem: Discuss the “Save Silent Valley Movement” as a success story. What was the issue, and how did people contribute to the conservation effort described ?
items.answer: The “Save Silent Valley Movement” successfully preserved a moist evergreen forest in Kerala, rich in biodiversity, from a proposed hydroelectric dam across the Kunthipuzha river. Common people, even those not residing nearby, led a decade-long battle. They used widespread awareness programs, letters to editors, newspaper articles, seminars, and legal petitions to voice their opposition. This collective public effort was instrumental in saving the Silent Valley and its unique ecosystem from destruction.

items.stem: Who was Salim Ali, and what were his significant contributions to the understanding and conservation of bird diversity in India ?
items.answer: Salim Ali, known as the ‘Birdman of India’, was an ornithologist who travelled extensively across India to observe bird diversity. He meticulously prepared lists of birds, documented their travel routes and habitats, and identified regions with high bird diversity. Crucially, he took measures to conserve these regions, with Keoladeo National Park and Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary being examples he helped preserve. His landmark series of 10 books on Indian subcontinent birds also significantly contributed to ornithology.

items.stem: A group of students observed two different types of plants in their school garden. Plant A was short with a soft, green stem and leaves showing veins running parallel to each other. Plant B was much taller, with a hard, thick, woody brown stem, and its leaves had a net-like pattern of veins. They also found some seeds near Plant B which, when opened, split into two parts. (i) Based on the stem characteristics, classify Plant A and Plant B. (ii) What type of leaf venation does Plant A likely have? What about Plant B? (iii) Based on the seed structure found near Plant B and its leaf venation, what type of root system would Plant B most likely possess? (iv) If Plant A is a type of grass, would its root system more likely be taproot or fibrous? Explain.
items.answer: (i) Plant A, being short with a soft, green stem, is likely a herb. Plant B, being tall with a hard, thick, woody brown stem, is a tree. (ii) Plant A, with veins running parallel, has parallel venation. Plant B, with a net-like pattern of veins, has reticulate venation. (iii) Plant B’s seeds split into two parts (dicot), and its leaves have reticulate venation. Therefore, Plant B would most likely possess a taproot system. (iv) If Plant A is a type of grass (which typically has parallel venation), it would more likely have a fibrous root system, as monocots generally have parallel venation and fibrous roots.

items.stem: In a documentary, students saw camels surviving in the extremely hot desert of Rajasthan and also different camels in the cold, mountainous desert of Ladakh. The narrator explained that the features of these camels help them live in their respective environments. For instance, the Rajasthan camel has very long legs and one hump, while the Ladakh camel has shorter legs and two humps. (i) What is the general term for features that help animals survive in their specific environments? (ii) How do the long legs of the Rajasthan camel likely help it in the hot sandy desert? (iii) Why might the Ladakh camel benefit from having two humps compared to the single hump of the Rajasthan camel, considering food availability? (iv) Besides leg length and number of humps, suggest one other physical adaptation a Ladakh camel might have for cold conditions, based on the chapter’s information.
items.answer: (i) The general term for features that help animals survive in their specific environments is adaptations. (ii) The long legs of the Rajasthan camel, along with wide hooves, help it walk on the sandy desert without sinking into the sand and keep its body further from the hot ground. (iii) Camels store food in their humps. Having two humps might provide the Ladakh camel with a larger food reserve, which is beneficial as food can be very scarce in the cold desert, especially during late winters when these humps shrink. (iv) The Ladakh camel grows long hair from head to neck, which is an adaptation to help it survive the extreme cold winters of its mountainous desert habitat.

items.stem: A science class was studying biodiversity. The teacher displayed pictures of a fish, a frog, and a squirrel. She asked students to think about where these animals live and how they are suited to their surroundings. The fish was shown swimming in water, the frog near a pond, and the squirrel on a tree. (i) Classify the habitats of the fish and the squirrel as either terrestrial or aquatic. (ii) What term is used for animals like frogs that can live both in water and on land? (iii) What features does a fish possess that are adaptations for living in water, as mentioned in the chapter? (iv) Why is it important that these different animals live in habitats suited to their features?
items.answer: (i) The fish’s habitat (water) is aquatic. The squirrel’s habitat (on a tree/land) is terrestrial. (ii) Animals like frogs that can live both in water and on land are called amphibians. (iii) Fish have streamlined bodies and fins, which are adaptations that help them to swim and move efficiently in water. (iv) It is important because their specific features (adaptations) are tailored for survival in those particular environments, providing them with food, shelter, and the means to reproduce successfully.

items.stem: Students were discussing Project Tiger. They learned it was initiated because the Bengal Tiger population was declining due to habitat loss. Their teacher explained that many such projects are needed because when habitats are damaged, it affects not just one species but the entire variety of life in that area. (i) What was the primary reason for the decline in the Bengal Tiger population that led to “Project Tiger”? (ii) What is the term for the variety of life in a particular area? (iii) According to the chapter, what does damage to habitats lead to for plants and animals? (iv) Why is protecting habitats crucial for maintaining biodiversity?
items.answer: (i) The primary reason for the decline in the Bengal Tiger population was the loss of its natural habitat due to human activities. (ii) The term for the variety of life in a particular area is biodiversity. (iii) Damage to habitats leads to plants and animals losing their homes, food, and other essential resources for survival. (iv) Protecting habitats is crucial because habitats provide everything plants and animals need to survive; without healthy habitats, species cannot thrive, leading to a reduction in the overall variety of life.

items.stem: During a lesson on plant classification, a teacher showed students a chickpea seed that could be split into two parts and a maize seed that was a single unit. She then showed them the leaves of a chickpea plant which had a net-like vein pattern, and maize leaves which had veins running side- by-side. (i) Based on its seed structure, is a chickpea plant a monocot or a dicot? (ii) What type of leaf venation is characteristic of the chickpea plant, according to the observation? (iii) Based on its seed structure (single unit), what type of leaf venation would you expect a maize plant to have? (iv) What type of root system is generally associated with plants like chickpea (dicot with reticulate venation)?
items.answer: (i) A chickpea seed splits into two parts (cotyledons), so a chickpea plant is a dicotyledon (dicot). (ii) The chickpea plant, with a net-like vein pattern, exhibits reticulate venation. (Implied by “net-like”) (iii) A maize seed is a single unit (monocot), so you would expect a maize plant to have parallel leaf venation. (iv) Plants like chickpea (dicots with reticulate venation) are generally associated with a taproot system.
